Subject: Post-call recap & acceptance criteria — JuniperAI integration

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side to make sure we aligned on the technical requirements and next steps. Please flag anything I’ve missed or mischaracterized.

High-level goals you shared:
- Replace on-prem KG lookup with an LLM-based reranking layer to improve relevance by ~15–20% across search use cases.
- Keep 95th/99th percentile latency within strict bounds for UI-serving flows (real-time suggestions).
- Minimize token cost for high-volume endpoints (customer-facing QA) while keeping answer fidelity.

Key non-functional acceptance criteria (agreed in-call):
- Latency: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 420ms for 256-token prompts under sustained load for the primary endpoint.
- Throughput: baseline steady-state 40 req/s per endpoint with ability to burst to 120 req/s for short windows (<= 90s).
- Availability: 99.9% for the endpoint during business hours (US PST) with automatic fallback to a smaller model when throughput pressure causes degradation.
- Cost target: reduce current per-request cost by >= 25% vs your managed provider baseline (we'll validate once we see traces/usage).

Model & input constraints:
- Primary model family: causal Llama-compat 13B-70B family — you indicated preference for a quantized 4-bit variant for cost/latency tradeoff.
- Average prompt size: 180 tokens; 95th percentile ~320 tokens.
- Expected KV cache reuse: medium (prefixes repeat across customer sessions).

Topology options we discussed:
1) Dedicated VPC deployment (recommended for first phase): private Redwood Private control plane, dedicated GPU pool (mixed A10p / H100 depending on cost curve), per-customer autoscaling to meet p95/p99 SLOs.
2) Hosted + Dedicated hybrid: primary traffic to Dedicated, spillover to Hosted instances during unexpected spikes (with model variant downgrade).

Immediate artifacts we agreed to exchange:
- JuniperAI: sample traces (last 7 days), distribution of prompt lengths, current p95/p99 numbers, and Spike/peak windows (action: Alex) — due EOD 2028-04-03.
- Redwood: initial SLO matrix and topology sketch (attachment), cost estimate for Dedicated pool and fallback hosted tier (action: Naomi / Marissa) — delivered by 2028-04-05.

Attachments included: SLO matrix (draft) and topology sketch — these are pointers for the post-call workshop.

Next proposed milestones:
- Week of 2028-04-08: 60-minute technical workshop (ops + infra) to review traces and validate KV cache expectations.
- 2028-04-15: mutual action plan (MAP) draft covering POC scope, success criteria, and timeline.

If all that looks right, Alex — can you send sample traces and a short note about peak windows? Priya — please confirm calendar availability for the 60-minute workshop week of 4/8.

Thanks again — feel free to edit inline.

—

Thanks Naomi — good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 420ms p99 number you called out is acceptable as a hard cap for the primary UI route, but for analytics/batch reranks we can tolerate p99 up to 1.2s. We will highlight which endpoints are UI vs batch in the traces.
- Average prompt length might be slightly larger than 180 tokens for customers using contextual history; 95th is closer to 420 tokens for those sessions. We will include the distribution.
- For the POC, we prefer the hybrid topology (Dedicated primary + Hosted failover) if the cost delta is reasonable.

Action: I will upload a zipped set of traces (anonymized) and a short CSV with token distributions by endpoint by EOD Monday (2028-04-03).

Adding a quick engineering note for clarity (copied into the thread so Juniper has context):

- KV cache expectations — if Juniper sessions reuse >40% prefix tokens across requests, we can achieve meaningful latency improvements via persistent KV caches pinned to the dedicated pool. If reuse is lower (<15%), benefit will be marginal and autoscaling must handle token compute.
- Model suggestions: start with a quantized 13B variant for the UI path (best p99/cost balance) and a 70B quantized variant only for the top-tier analytic jobs where latency is less strict.
- Prefetching: for the UI flow we recommend prefetching model KV for the top 50 active sessions during bursts to avoid cold starts — this is config in the deployment spec.

I'll prepare a short slide (1–2 pages) with the proposed deployment knobs for the workshop.

Karthik
